notes:
ACCESS: bedbathandbeyond.com is now Beyond Inc.'s (ex-Overstock) marketplace catalogue on a Next.js storefront. Direct fetches of /c/ listing pages are Akamai HTTP 403 through every one of probe.py's 10 curl_cffi fingerprints (re-confirmed this session on /c/bath). Two routes DO work and I used both. (1) The XML sitemaps are NOT protected and come back as genuine XML through probe.fetch directly - that is where the taxonomy comes from. (2) For listing pages, the route established by the prior Furniture pass on this SR still works: www-bedbathandbeyond-com.translate.goog/<path>?<orig query>&_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=es&_x_tr_hl=en, which returns the genuine server-rendered ORIGIN HTML including the complete __NEXT_DATA__ payload (1.3-1.8 MB per page). 90 distinct listing pages were read this way with zero failures; probe.py's 2s per-host gap plus a retry-with-backoff wrapper kept Google from 429-ing. EVERY link value recorded below is the canonical www.bedbathandbeyond.com origin URL taken verbatim from the site's own category sitemap - no translate.goog URL and no invented URL is recorded anywhere.

ROBOTS: https://www.bedbathandbeyond.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST, directly, HTTP 200. It names NO anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web / Claude-User agent. It does name Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, Sogou, TikTokSpider, Applebot, Amazonbot, Amzn-SearchBot, meta-externalagent, Mediapartners-Google (fully disallowed), Pinterestbot (Crawl-delay 0.2), GoogleOther (Disallow /c/*), PetalBot, Baiduspider (Disallow /c/*) and AhrefsBot. The 'User-Agent: *' block that applies here disallows /sm-*, /cart, /checkout, /productxml, /fs-bin/, /se/, /review-form.html, /addBundle, /US/es/*, /rentals/*, /cgi-bin/*, /item/*, /myaccount, /myreviews.html, /ip-status*, /profile/*, /*/product-answers.html, /*/product-questions.html, /Garage-Automotive/*, /shop/*, /registries/*, /trade/profile*, /api/apps/*, /apis/services/*, /api2/*, plus multi-parameter refinement patterns (/c/*?*&*&*&*&*&*, /*?*brand=*~*, /*?*price=*, /*?*products=*, /*~*~*, /*osp=*) and tracking paths. Every URL I requested is either a sitemap or a plain /c/<parent>/<child>?t=<id> category page with at most one added &page=N - none matches any Disallow pattern, and I issued no search, no /api/, no /shop/, no multi-facet refinement and no product-detail request. Declared sitemaps: /sitemap.xml (+ a second Sitemap line).

TREE - PRIMARY SOURCE: https://www.bedbathandbeyond.com/sitemap.xml -> https://www.bedbathandbeyond.com/sitemap/ctaxonomy/ctaxonomy.xml (HTTP 200, 136,965 bytes). This is the site's COMPLETE published category taxonomy: 1,430 category URLs, each of the form /c/<parent-slug>/<child-slug>?t=<taxonomy-id> (tier-1s are /c/<slug>?t=<id>), so the parent link is encoded in the URL itself. I parsed all 1,430 into a graph: 21 tier-1 departments (appliances, art, bath, bedding, furniture, games-puzzles, gifts, holiday, home-decor, home-improvement, housewares, kids-and-baby, kitchen-dining, lighting, luggage-bags, mattresses, office-supplies, outdoor, rugs, storage-organization, tools), zero orphans, and a maximum depth of 4. Grepping the 1,430 SLUG PATHS (host stripped - note that grepping the raw URLs is useless here because the hostname itself contains 'bath') for bath|shower|toilet|vanit|sink|basin|faucet|soap|towel|toothbrush|hamper|bidet|medicine|lavatory|plumb|robe returns 120 paths, and I triaged every one of them.

TREE - SECOND SOURCE (the site's own live nav): every /c/ page server-renders __NEXT_DATA__ -> props.pageProps.initialReduxState.pageData. Landing pages carry document.leftNav; listing pages carry facets[attributeGroupId='categories'].values, i.e. the site's own child-category list with canonical URLs and per-child counts. Both agree with the sitemap. The Bath department's leftNav (nav-level-1 template, no product grid, hence a grouping row) lists Towels, Bath Mats and Rugs, Shower Curtains and Accessories, Bathroom Accessories, Bath Trays and Caddies, Teak Bathroom Accessories (a &a1003=3463 FILTER url, excluded per rules 24/27), Bathrobes, Kids Bath, Beach Towels, Personal Care Appliances, 'Bathroom Renovation' -> /c/home-improvement/bathroom-fixtures?t=31169, and two promotional links (Shop Bath New Arrivals, Shop All Bath on Sale) excluded per rule 25. That leftNav is what proves the Bath department and the Home-Improvement bathroom tree are one bathroom assortment.

BATHROOM SCOPE ACTUALLY WALKED: 83 nodes, all HTTP 200. (a) Bath dept t=18647 and all 6 tier-2s and their children; (b) Home Improvement > Bathroom Fixtures t=31169 and all 8 tier-2s and their 19 children; (c) Furniture > Bathroom Furniture t=24355 and its 2 children; (d) Storage and Organization > Bathroom Storage t=70253; (e) Lighting > Bathroom Lighting t=31191 and its 2 children (routed out); (f) Kids > Kids' Bath t=18675 and its 5 children; (g) Baby > Baby Bath t=71406 and its 5 children; (h) Outdoor > Hot Tubs, Pools and Saunas > Outdoor Showers t=94429.

QTY SOURCE: pageData.resultCount, which is the number the page's own header renders. VERIFICATION 1 (header == resultCount): on all 72 of the walked nodes whose total is under the site's 5,000 display cap, the rendered header string matched resultCount EXACTLY - zero mismatches (e.g. Soap Dishes and Dispensers header '475' = resultCount 475; Towel Racks '1,053' = 1053; Bathroom Vanity Mirrors '1,021' = 1021). The 7 nodes over the cap render no plain number in the header (Bathroom Fixtures 37,786; Bathroom Furniture 17,024; Bathroom Vanities 13,613; Bathroom Lighting 9,302; Showers and Bathtubs 7,132; Bathroom Hardware 6,904; Bathroom Sinks and Faucets 5,869) - for the one of those that is a recorded LEAF, Bathroom Vanities, the figure cited is the page's own resultCount. VERIFICATION 2 (JSON-LD): each listing page also emits schema.org ItemList numberOfItems equal to resultCount (spot-checked, e.g. Soap Dishes and Dispensers numberOfItems 475). VERIFICATION 3 (independent partition proofs - the strongest evidence here): the parent's category-facet counts, the children's own page counts, and the parent's resultCount agree exactly on three different branches. Bathroom Accessories: parent resultCount 2,529, and its 17 facet children (475+349+222+189+187+177+151+132+126+124+93+72+70+61+54+33+14) sum to EXACTLY 2,529, with every facet count identical to that child's own page count - a perfect, residue-free partition of 17 leaves. Shower Curtains and Accessories: 1,461+111+109+44 = 1,725 = parent exactly. Bathroom Sinks and Faucets: 3,179+2,593+97(cross-listed mounted soap dispensers) = 5,869 = parent exactly. Kids' Bath: 35+24+18+12+5 = 94 = parent exactly. Baby Bath: 423+172+12 = 607 = parent exactly. VERIFICATION 4 (exhaustion): I paginated Grab Bars (reported 278) to the end - &page=1..5 returned 80/81/81/81/38 rendered slots yielding 277 UNIQUE product ids (the surplus slots are sponsored tiles repeating organic products), and &page=6 fell back to currentPage=1, confirming 5 pages is the end. 277 unique vs a reported 278 is a single-item discrepancy from one sponsored/organic duplicate; the site's own figure 278 is what is recorded, and the 1-item gap is disclosed here rather than smoothed over. Page size is 60 organic and pagination is internally consistent everywhere: Toilet Brushes 54 -> 1 page, Bathroom Wall Shelves 44 -> 1 page, Grab Bars 278 -> 5 pages = ceil(278/60). VERIFICATION 5 (discrimination): the 47 recorded leaf counts range from 5 to 13,613 and are all different figures - no site-wide constant - and every page's taxonomyName and JSON-LD breadcrumb matched the node requested.

COUNT DRIFT, DISCLOSED: the child counts shown in the Bathroom Fixtures page's category facet were read minutes before each child's own page, and 7 of them are 1-2% lower than the child's own later reading (vanities 13,386 vs 13,613; hardware 6,780 vs 6,904; sinks-faucets 5,767 vs 5,869; showers-bathtubs 7,018 vs 7,132; toilets-bidets 1,805 vs 1,831; wall cabinets 1,356 vs 1,372; vanity mirrors 999 vs 1,021). This is live marketplace inventory drift on a catalogue of this size. In every case the recorded figure is the NODE'S OWN page reading, never the parent's facet number, per the no-reuse-of-a-parent's-number rule.

PARENT-URL / NO-AGGREGATION DISCIPLINE (rule 24): Bath (18647), Bathroom Accessories (18656), Shower Curtains and Accessories (18666), Bathroom Fixtures (31169), Bathroom Hardware (31203), Bathroom Sinks and Faucets (31198), Showers and Bathtubs (31195), Toilets and Bidets (31197), Bathroom Furniture (24355) and Kids' Bath (18675) all have valid child listings, so each is a GROUPING row with blank qty and blank link and none of their totals is recorded. Bathroom Furniture deserves a specific note: its 17,024 is a pure roll-up - its category facet resolves entirely into Bathroom Vanities 13,613, Linen Towers 1,534, Bathroom Wall Cabinets 1,372, Vanity Stools 222, Shower Stools 177, Over-the-Toilet Storage 165 and Bathroom Wall Shelves 44, every one of which is already recorded under its own canonical parent - so only its two OWN taxonomy children (Linen Towers, Over-the-Toilet Storage) appear beneath it and the 17,024 is discarded. The same roll-up caveat for Bathroom Storage is spelled out in review.

CROSS-LISTING NOTED, NOT DUPLICATED: BB&B's category facet is 'categories present in this result set', not strictly 'children', so several nodes surface under more than one parent. Shower Curtain Rods and Shower Curtain Hooks appear in the Bathroom Hardware facet as well as under Shower Curtains and Accessories; Towel Warmers appears under both Bathroom Accessories and Bathroom Hardware; Bathroom Fans appears under both Bathroom Lighting and Bathroom Hardware; mounted soap dispensers (a Kitchen node) appears under Bathroom Sinks and Faucets; Wall Sconces (4,345) appears under Bathroom Lighting; cabinet-hardware (1,988) and drawer-pulls (162) appear under Bathroom Hardware; Outdoor Showers appears under Showers and Bathtubs. The general Hardware nodes (cabinet hardware, drawer pulls) and the Kitchen soap-dispenser node were NOT recorded - they are kitchen/general hardware by primary type and hierarchy.

RESULT: 53 rows - 11 grouping rows and 42 leaves, every leaf carrying the site's own exact figure and its canonical origin URL - plus 23 review entries: five cross-file dedup exclusions, everything routed to Textile (11 nodes), everything routed to Lighting (3 nodes), one excluded personal-care branch, one low-confidence baby node, one overlap disclosure and one empty node.
